post_rebuild_reparse.method: civds.civilization.parse_civilization_records() run directly against the rebuilt ROM's ARM9 image (the rebuilt image no longer matches the pinned exact-ROM profile by design, so `civds civilization summarize` correctly refuses it; this step re-verifies behavior with the same parser used by that command, called directly)

conclusion: A guarded civilization patch manifest (renaming civilization 9's leader from Napoleon to Louis, in place within the packed leader-name string pool) was generated from the real ROM, applied to an extracted workspace (already carrying the earlier technology-table e2e patch in this session), rebuilt into a new ROM, and re-parsed - confirming exactly the targeted leader changed and every other civilization's name, index, and pointer stayed intact. This proves the full leader-name table discovery (anchor -> pointer array -> packed string pool with derived per-slot capacity) end to end as a real modding capability, not just a static analysis claim.
